name: How does the average price of products purchased by a customer change over their lifetime?
python_code:
# Filter out rows with missing Customer ID and negative/zero Quantity (returns/cancellations)
df_clean = df.dropna(subset=['Customer ID']).copy()
df_clean = df_clean[df_clean['Quantity'] > 0].copy()

# Convert InvoiceDate to datetime
df_clean['InvoiceDate'] = pd.to_datetime(df_clean['InvoiceDate'])

# Sort by Customer ID and InvoiceDate to establish purchase order
df_clean = df_clean.sort_values(['Customer ID', 'InvoiceDate']).reset_index(drop=True)

# For each customer, assign a purchase sequence number based on invoice date
# Group by Customer ID and Invoice to get per-invoice average price
invoice_avg_price = df_clean.groupby(['Customer ID', 'Invoice'])['Price'].mean().reset_index()
invoice_avg_price = invoice_avg_price.rename(columns={'Price': 'AvgInvoicePrice'})

# Get the first invoice date per customer-invoice to order purchases
invoice_dates = df_clean[['Customer ID', 'Invoice', 'InvoiceDate']].drop_duplicates()
invoice_avg_price = invoice_avg_price.merge(invoice_dates, on=['Customer ID', 'Invoice'])

# Sort by customer and date, then assign purchase number
invoice_avg_price = invoice_avg_price.sort_values(['Customer ID', 'InvoiceDate']).reset_index(drop=True)
invoice_avg_price['PurchaseNumber'] = invoice_avg_price.groupby('Customer ID').cumcount() + 1

# Calculate average price per purchase number across all customers
result = invoice_avg_price.groupby('PurchaseNumber')['AvgInvoicePrice'].mean().reset_index()
result = result.rename(columns={'AvgInvoicePrice': 'AveragePrice'})
